title: Internal sync batch trusts unvalidated year and term from JSON

evidence.quote: const { year, term, subjects, status, totalSubjects } = await c.req.json...; ... if (!subjects || !Array.isArray(subjects) || subjects.length === 0) ...
const result = await syncSubjects(... year, term, subjects, ...); ... status: resolveManualSyncTermStatus(existingTerm, requestedStatus),

reasoning: The TypeScript body type does not validate runtime JSON. The route validates subjects, status, and totalSubjects, but then uses arbitrary year and term values to sync subjects and upsert term_state. A malformed authenticated internal request can create bogus term IDs/counts or target an unintended upstream path.
recommendation: Validate year as an integer in the supported range and term against the known TERMS set before calling syncSubjects or upserting term_state. Consider validating subject codes and capping internal batch length as well.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included sync-batch tests use valid year and term payloads and focus on cumulative counts and skipped batches; they do not send malformed year or term values.
suggestedRegressionTest: POST /internal/sync-batch with {"year":"2026","term":"autumn","subjects":["CS"],"totalSubjects":1} should return 400 and not call syncSubjects or upsertTermState.
minimumFixScope: Add runtime validation in apps/api/src/routes/sync.ts before constructing config or calling syncSubjects.
